summary: André Wedemeyer was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and history and archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor August Conrady around 1905–1909 and held a post at Leipzig University.

André-Georges Haudricourt was a linguist and Sinologist who studied at the Institut national agronomique, under Marcel Mauss, and at Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He held positions at the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle, CNRS, EFEO, and Paris Descartes University.

Andy Rotman works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, later holding posts at Smith College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and held a professorship at Rutgers University, attested in 2005.
Angela Manderscheid is a scholar in Tibetology and related fields. She has held posts at the Free University of Berlin and at the University of Oulu, where she was attested as a researcher in 1998.

Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa, studying under Nalini Devdas, and served as an assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities.

Angela Zito is a scholar in Sinology and religious studies who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (1980–1989). Around 2000, she became an associate professor of anthropology and religious studies at New York University.

Angelika Krebs is a philosopher who studied at Freiburg, New College, Konstanz, Berkeley, and Goethe University Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt, and Basel, where she took the chair for practical philosophy in 2001.

Angelika Malinar works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. After studies and habilitation at Mainz and Tübingen, she held teaching posts at the Free University of Berlin and SOAS, becoming Associate Professor of Indology at the University of Zurich in 2009.

Angelo De Gubernatis was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (from 1890).
Anil Kumar is a scholar working in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Hyderabad by 2012 and subsequently held a post there.

Anil Vidyalankar is an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi, and founded Sandhaan in 1988, serving as its director.
Ankita Chakraborty is an Indology researcher who studied under doctoral supervisor Bijoya Goswami. Attested in 2026, she holds a position as a Research Scholar/Fellow at the Asiatic Society.

Ankur Barua is an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and the University of Hong Kong under Dorothy C. Wong. He held a post at the University of Delhi.

Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 1983, she completed a Master of Arts at the Australian National University under the supervision of Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at Rice University under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal, attested in 2010.

Ann Grodzins Gold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She completed her B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. in anthropology at the University of Chicago (1973–1984) and held posts at Cornell University and Syracuse University.

Ann Heirman is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research from 1995 to 2009 and at Ghent University as a permanent member and director from 2003 to 2012.

Ann Laura Stoler is a historian who earned degrees at Barnard College and Columbia University. She held teaching positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Michigan before becoming founding director at The New School in 2004.

Anna Andreeva is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She has held posts at Heidelberg University and Ghent University, where she is attested as a permanent member in 2026.
